fields.meta_title: RFQ Form Builder for Supplier Quotes | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build an RFQ form that sends one line-item request to every supplier, closes at your deadline and puts the returned quotes side by side.
fields.h1: Build an RFQ Form That Puts Supplier Quotes Side by Side
fields.hero_description: List what you need priced and the terms that apply. Emergent builds the RFQ form your suppliers answer and lines up every quote in one grid when it closes.
fields.features_heading: The Buyer's Side of Every Quote
fields.features_subheading: A spreadsheet RFQ comes back in as many layouts as you have suppliers. A form keeps every price in the same column.
fields.feature_1:
Line items nobody can misread

Give each item a quantity and a unit, and attach a drawing where one exists. Every supplier then prices the same lines in the same fields instead of sending its own layout.
fields.feature_2:
A private link for each supplier

Invite suppliers by email, each with a link to its own response page. A supplier sees only its own bid, and your list shows which invited suppliers have replied and which have not.
fields.feature_3:
A due time the form enforces

Set the response deadline to the hour. The form stops taking quotes once it passes, and each bid records the minute it arrived, settling any argument about a late supplier.
fields.feature_4:
Bids side by side, line by line

Put every supplier's price for every line in one grid with line totals. The lowest price on each line is marked, and a split award across suppliers is priced before you pick it.
fields.feature_5:
Terms that sit next to the price

Ask each supplier for its lead time and how long its price holds. Answers sit beside each total, and a cheap quote with a ten-week lead time stands out before anyone awards it.
fields.feature_6:
Your RFQ app, in your repository

Export the full code to your GitHub repository whenever you want it. Every past bid and award decision then stays in a codebase your purchasing team owns and can extend.
fields.why_title: Why Build RFQ Forms With Emergent?
fields.why_description: Emailed spreadsheets leave someone retyping supplier prices into one sheet. A form collects them there from the first reply.

fields.tab_content_1:
Box prices compared one line at a time

Fernhill Foods buys shipping cartons in three sizes: 20,000 small, 12,000 medium and 6,000 large. One RFQ goes to three packaging suppliers, who each enter a unit price per size. Ridgeback Packaging has the lowest single bid at $21,420. Taking each size from its cheapest supplier costs $20,700, or $720 less.
fields.tab_content_2:
Every line priced, or the bid goes back

Holloway Homes sends a 14-line materials list for a townhome project to four lumber yards, due Friday at 5:00 p.m. Each line names a quantity and a grade. Bayside Lumber priced 12 of the 14 lines. The form marked its bid incomplete and emailed the yard the two lines it skipped.
fields.tab_content_3:
Ashford wins on all-in rate, not on base rate

Corwin Home Goods ships weekly between Dallas and Atlanta and asks five carriers to quote the lane. Each enters a base rate and a fuel surcharge per load, and the form adds them into one all-in rate. Northline Freight's base is $70 lower, but it comes to $2,160 all in. Ashford Transport takes the lane at $2,110.
fields.tab_content_4:
Five days to order before a price lapses

Dana Ruiz runs IT at Brennan Shaw and needs 60 laptops and 60 docks. Three resellers quote through the form, each price valid for 30 days. Orbit Systems wins at $71,400. If no purchase order has gone out five days before that quote expires, Dana gets an email with the quote and a link to raise the order.

fields.howto_title: How to Make an RFQ Form
fields.howto_description: Settle exactly what you are buying before anyone prices it. The form can only compare what you defined.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List the items before the suppliers
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Fix the terms every quote must use
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Set a due hour and a validity period
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pin down each line with a description and a quantity, and attach any spec or drawing that defines it. Suppliers can only quote what you define, and a vague line comes back priced three different ways.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Name the delivery address, the date the goods must arrive on site and the payment terms you expect. When every supplier quotes on identical terms, unit prices compare directly and nobody wins on a cheaper shipping assumption.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Give an exact hour for responses, such as 3:00 p.m. Eastern, and ask how long each price holds, for example 45 days. A price that lapses before your purchase order goes out has to be quoted again.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Send the request to at least three suppliers who already meet your quality and delivery needs. An RFQ compares price. Screen for capability before the request goes out, because a low bid from a supplier who cannot deliver is no saving.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste the line items and terms into one prompt with the deadline and supplier emails. Emergent builds the response form and invitation emails, plus the comparison grid. Change any field later by asking in a sentence.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Choose before bids open whether the whole list goes to one supplier or each line goes to its lowest price. Have the app price both options, then email the winner and tell the other suppliers the result.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Run a dry round with a colleague
fields.howto_step_7_des: Have a colleague open the invitation on a phone and price every line but one. Check that the blank line is flagged and the arrival time is stored. Delete the test bid before the real invitations go out.

plan.angle: The live top 10 mixes supplier pages that take quote requests (ASC Process Systems, TelAztec, HelloForms), government RFQ PDFs from Santa Rosa and Tennessee, a freight RFQ post and a WordPress form tutorial, while the image pack and AI Overview point to Word and Excel templates. None shows the buyer's side once the RFQ goes out: one line-item request sent to several suppliers, every price returned in the same fields before a deadline, and the bids compared line by line. This page answers the People Also Ask questions on what an RFQ is, what it contains and how it differs from an RFP and RFI, then shows four buyers whose RFQ form does the comparison: a food maker pricing cartons by size, a home builder catching an incomplete lumber bid, a shipper ranking carriers on all-in rate and an IT manager warned before a reseller's quote expires. A seller's own quote request page stays on the quote form sibling, linked from the FAQ.

claims_to_source: A quotation is not an offer and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract; the order is the offer, and a contract is established when the supplier accepts it
RFIs may be used when the Government does not presently intend to award a contract but wants price, delivery, other market information or capabilities for planning, and responses are not offers
Responses to requests for proposals are offers called proposals, while responses to requests for quotations are quotations, not offers
Government buyers on GSA eBuy post RFQs as line items and can include attachments such as a statement of work
Requests for proposals describe the requirement, the anticipated terms, the information the proposal must contain and the evaluation factors with their relative importance
